# TabDesk

> A Linux desktop application for working with many terminals at once. Every
> project directory becomes a tab with its own embedded terminal; each project
> chooses which CLI that terminal starts, and a tab turns green when its
> terminal has been quiet for a moment.

Site: https://tabdesk.thern.io/
Author: Jonaz Thern (info@thern.io, https://thern.io)
Version: 0.1.13 · MIT licence

## What it is

TabDesk is a desktop window that arranges several real terminals side by side,
one per project, and tells you which of them has stopped producing output. It is
not a terminal emulator and not a multiplexer: each panel is an actual xterm
window reparented into the panel through X11, so anything that works in a
terminal works there — curses apps, colour, mouse reporting, ssh, tcpdump.

## Which CLIs it runs

A project chooses what its terminal starts, and the choice is remembered with
the project. TabDesk offers only the CLIs actually installed on the machine,
found by looking them up on PATH:

- Claude Code (Anthropic) — started with `--permission-mode auto`, and the only
  one TabDesk passes a per-project model flag to
- Codex (OpenAI)
- Gemini CLI (Google)
- opencode
- Aider
- Cursor Agent
- A plain shell — no agent at all

## The your-turn signal

TabDesk measures how many bytes each terminal writes. A background tab pulses
while output is flowing and turns green once it has been quiet for a moment.
Because the signal comes from output rather than from the program, it flags a
finished agent, a finished build and a finished rsync the same way.

## Requirements

- Linux running X11. Wayland is not supported: the embedded terminals rely on
  X11 window reparenting, which Wayland does not allow.
- xterm and xdotool for the terminals, python3-gi for reading GTK colours. All
  are pulled in by the package.

## Other features

- Grid view of one to six terminals at once
- Live preview: runs the project (static HTML, Node, Python, Rust, Go) next to
  the terminal and renders it, with element inspection on hover
- Colours derived from the running GTK theme and interface language from the
  system locale, both updating live
- A system bar with token usage for agents that report it, plus CPU, RAM, clock

## Availability

TabDesk is publicly available under the MIT licence.

- Source: https://github.com/TheJonaz/tabdesk
- Apt repository: https://cdn.thern.io/tabdesk (signed; stable main)
- Install instructions: https://cdn.thern.io/tabdesk/install.html
- Tarball, for machines without apt: https://cdn.thern.io/tabdesk/

The quickest install fetches the signing key, verifies its fingerprint before
writing it, adds the source and installs:

    curl -fsSL https://cdn.thern.io/tabdesk/install.sh | sudo bash

Updates then arrive with apt upgrade, or through the update chip in TabDesk's
own system bar.
